Susan Smith denied parole again 32 years after drowning her two sons
- Published
A South Carolina woman who admitted to drowning her two sons 32 years ago has been denied parole for a second time.
Susan Smith, 55, was convicted of killing her boys by strapping them into their car seats and rolling her vehicle into a lake in 1994.
"I got to my lowest when I let that car go into that lake," Smith said during a hearing on Thursday with the state board that decides whether to release those in prison on parole.
The board later unanimously turned down her request to be freed. The father of the two boys has vowed to continue to oppose her release, and several people spoke against her in the hearing.
Smith, whose lawyers had argued she suffered a mental breakdown during the crime, can apply to the South Carolina Board of Probation, Parole and Pardon Services for parole every two years.
According to CBS News, the BBC's US partner, she told the hearing that she had changed and matured since killing three-year-old Michael and one-year-old Alex. She also said she was "very, very sorry".
At her last hearing in 2024, her children's father, David Smith, said 30 years in prison was not a severe enough punishment.
"That's only 15 years per child, her own children," he said. "That's just not enough."
Prosecutors argued during the trial that Smith killed the boys after a man with whom she was having an affair told her that her sons were the reason that the pair did not have a future together.
At Thursday's hearing, Smith said: "This did not happen because of a man. That's just not true."
When the boys first disappeared, Smith said she was carjacked late at night and a man drove away with her car. While she pleaded publicly for their safe return, her sons were at the bottom of a nearby lake.
But ultimately she confessed to the crime.
Defence lawyers said she had wanted to die with her children but left the car at the last minute.
Smith was convicted of murder, but under South Carolina law at the time, she was eligible for a parole hearing every two years after serving 30 years in prison.
In the US, some people convicted of crimes are eligible for parole, which means they can be released from incarceration.
She would have needed two-thirds of the board members present to vote in her favour to be freed.

digest_he:
סוזן סמית', אישה מדרום קרוליינה שהודתה בהטבעת שני בניה לפני 32 שנים, נדחתה פה אחד בבקשתה השנייה לשחרור מוקדם על ידי ועדת השחרורים המדינתית. סמית' בת ה-55 ריצתה עונש מאסר לאחר שהורשעה ברצח בני ובנותיה הקטנים ב-1994, לאחר שקשרה אותם למושבי הרכב והידרדרה איתו לתוך אגם.

במהלך השימוע טענה סמית' כי השתנתה והיא מצטערת מאוד על מעשיה, ואף הכחישה את הטענה שהרצח נבע מקשר רומנטי שהיה לו בזמנו. מנגד, אבי הילדים וגורמי תביעה התנגדו בחריפות לשחרורה, וטענו ששלושים שנות מאסר אינן עונש מספיק עבור רצח הילדים.

סמית' תוכל להגיש בקשת שחרור נוספת פעם בשתיים שנים בהתאם לחוק במדינה. למרות טענות ההגנה על התמוטטות נפשית בעת ביצוע המעשה, ועדת השחרורים החליטה שלא להיענות לבקשתה.
